Lumber merchant at Fort Covington, where he and his brother Frederick ran the lumber business —
the first DeWitt in the family, named for Governor DeWitt Clinton of the Erie Canal,
just 22 years after it opened. He and Frederick married sisters, Grace and Nellie Southworth of Bangor.
He died in 1912 and lies at Elmwood Cemetery, Fort Covington, under a stone that also carries Grace’s name,
its death year never finished: she later married George W. Anderson, lived at Clarkston,
Washington, and is buried at Palouse.
